summary: Pandemic is a tense cooperative puzzle where players jointly plan efficient routes and role synergies to cure four diseases before outbreaks chain into a loss; the deck's escalating epidemic cards create a tightening clock that forces constant re-prioritization. Turns are short and mechanical, but the shared threat produces a lot of table talk and quarterbacking as the group tries to optimize the group's actions.
praised: Tense, escalating difficulty curve from epidemic cards and the infection rate track
Strong cooperative puzzle-solving and role synergy (variable player powers)
Approachable rules for a co-op game, quick to teach
High replayability from variable setup and roles
Genuine nail-biting tension near the end of a game
criticised: Prone to 'quarterbacking' where one player dictates everyone's moves
Can feel solved/repetitive after many plays since optimal strategy emerges
Randomness (epidemic card draws, city card draws) can swing a well-played game to a loss
Low personal agency once a dominant player takes over group decisions
Some find the theme thin/abstracted despite the medical setting

interaction.kind: cooperative planning and negotiation, no conflict

scoring.why: The group wins or loses together based solely on curing all four diseases before running out of player cards, outbreaks (8), or infection cards.
